name: Michael Gans
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Jacques Gans is a Luxembourgish-American businessman who owns commercial real estate in Dublin, London, Luxembourg and Manchester.

He used to own 25% of logistics firm Supreme Group, with the rest held by his business partner Stephen Orenstein. Supreme Group was the primary supplier of food and water to the U.S. army in Afghanistan.
The firm was founded in 1957 to supply food to U.S. military bases in Germany by Orenstein's father Alfred, a former U.S. army soldier. Gans joined the company after Orenstein took over in 1985.

name: Teresita Sy-Coson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Teresita Sy-Coson is vice chairperson of SM Investments, one of the country's largest conglomerates started by her late father Henry Sy.
She is the eldest child of the group's founder.
Her SM experience spans retail merchandising, mall development and banking.
She also serves as the chairperson of BDO Unibank, a retail bank.
Her husband was Chinese lumber tycoon Louis Coson who died in 2003.
forbes_facts: Her father discouraged her from graduate studies and said, "Come work with me; it's the school of hard knocks."
At age 22 she helped open SM's first department store in Manila.
In 2022, SM Investments agreed to acquire Philippine Geothermal Production in a $304 million, all-share deal in a bid to lower its carbon footprint.

name: Oliver Samwer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2024)
forbes_bio: Oliver Samwer and his brothers Alexander and Marc founded Berlin-based tech incubator Rocket Internet in 2007 and took it public in October 2014.
Oliver is the middle brother and the CEO of Rocket Internet, which delisted from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in October 2020.
Together, the Samwers own around 45% of Rocket. The company was valued at more than $8 billion at the time of its IPO.
Inspired by the dot-com boom, they created a German auction site, Alando, in 1999 and sold it to eBay for $43 million after a few months.
That was followed by the creation of mobile phone content provider Jamba!, which they sold to Verisign in 2004 for $273 million.
forbes_facts: Oliver once said in an interview that he has no time for hobbies, preferring to spend his spare time with his children.

name: Paul Little
forbes_bio: Paul Little founded and chairs the Little Group, which has interests in property, investments, philanthropy, aviation and lifestyle.
He ran logistics firm Toll Holdings for 26 years and then got a boost in his wealth when Japan Post bought Toll.
Now he's focused on Melbourne apartment developments through his Little Projects.
He built a corporate jet base and is competing with Australian billionaire Lindsay Fox for customers.
forbes_facts: He is a former chairman of the Essendon Football Club.

name: Thomas Meyer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2014-2019); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Thomas Meyer is founder and CEO of Spanish retailer Desigual.
Meyer started the company in 1984 with a denim jacket created from a patchwork of worn blue jeans.
The first store opened in Ibiza in 1986. There are now over 500 stores in 33 countries around the world.
In 2014, French investment firm Eurazeo purchased a 10% stake in the retailer.
Meyer appears to have spent more than $160 million to take back full control of the company in 2018.

name: Ashok Soota
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun Global (2022-2024)
forbes_bio: IT veteran Ashok Soota gets his wealth from a majority stake in Bangalore-based tech firm Happiest Minds Technologies.
Soota worked at fellow billionaire Azim Premji's software giant Wipro before striking out on his own with IT provider Mindtree.
Mindtree was acquired by engineering firm Larsen & Toubro in a hostile takeover in 2019.
Soota moved out of Mindtree in 2011 to set up Happiest Minds that same year, along with nine cofounders. He took it public in 2020.
In April 2021, he launched  Scientific Knowledge for Ageing and Neurological Ailments (SKAN), a nonprofit organization focused on medical research related to aging and neurological disorders.
forbes_facts: Soota is on the board of governors of his alma mater, the Asian Institute Management in the Philippines.
He loves yoga, taichi and trekking.

name: Ching Bor Tung
forbes_bio: Tung is the vice chairman of Xinyi Glass, a supplier of glass for the automobile, construction and household good industries.
Tung Ching Bor is the brother of Tung Ching Sai, who is also a billionaire.
Tung Ching Bor is the brother-in-law of Lee Yin Yee, Xinyi's chairman and a fellow billionaire.
